items.text: Explain what AWS RDS is and why it's called 'managed'
Name all 6 database engines supported by RDS
Explain the difference between Multi-AZ and Read Replicas — purpose, replication type, and use case
Describe how Aurora's distributed storage works and how it differs from standard RDS
Explain OLTP vs OLAP and which AWS service handles each
Describe how ElastiCache works — cache hit vs cache miss flow
Compare Redis vs Memcached and know when to use each
Explain what DMS is and differentiate homogeneous vs heterogeneous migration
Create an RDS MySQL instance with correct security group settings
Connect an EC2 application to an RDS database using the endpoint
Place RDS in a private subnet and EC2 in a public subnet within a VPC
Write and schedule a Linux cron job to automate file movement to S3
Host a static website on S3 and serve it via CloudFront
Identify the correct AWS database service given a scenario description
Answer: Multi-AZ = high availability / synchronous / cannot read from standby
Answer: Read Replicas = read scaling / asynchronous / can be promoted / up to 5 (RDS) or 15 (Aurora)
Answer: Aurora = MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible / 3-5x faster / 6 copies across 3 AZs / failover < 30s
Answer: Redshift = data warehouse / OLAP / MPP / columnar storage / terabyte to petabyte
Answer: ElastiCache Redis = in-memory cache / supports persistence / backup / replication / complex data types
Answer: DMS = migrate databases to AWS / homogeneous (same engine) / heterogeneous (different engine + SCT)
Answer scenario: sub-millisecond reads + leaderboard = ElastiCache Redis
Answer scenario: 10 TB analytics + SQL BI tools = Redshift
